shortDescription: Replaces configured textures with a fully transparent texture. Useful to hide cosmetic textures from other mods (e.g., Create contraption hats).
oneLiner: Makes textures you list in the config invisible — either the whole image (the shipped default hides Create's contraption hats) or just a rectangle of it (the shipped default erases hat/accessory areas from zombie skins) — without editing a single file on disk.

configKeys.effect: List of texture ResourceLocations to replace with a fully transparent 1x1 PNG (format: namespace:textures/category/name.png). Entries are accepted by the config validator if they merely contain ":"; entries that ResourceLocation.tryParse cannot parse are silently dropped at read time.

configKeys.defaultValue: 62 entries covering 38 distinct texture files (TextureKillConfig.DEFAULT_ERASED_REGIONS, lines 23-90), e.g. "minecraft:textures/entity/zombie/drowned.png@32:0-64:16"
configKeys.effect: List of rectangular texture regions to erase (make transparent) inside an otherwise untouched texture (format: namespace:textures/path.png@x1:y1-x2:y2, end coordinates exclusive; repeat the same path with different @-suffixes for multiple regions — getErasedRegions() groups them per ResourceLocation). Validator only requires the string to contain ":" and "@".

events: net.neoforged.neoforge.event.AddPackFindersEvent (MOD bus, Dist.CLIENT — TextureKillClientEvents.onAddPackFinders; early-returns unless event.getPackType() == PackType.CLIENT_RESOURCES)
notes:
PROVABLE MECHANICS
- Two independent mechanisms, one config key each:
  1. killed_textures → a virtual client resource pack ("vanillaplusadditions:texture_kill", display name Component.literal("VPA Texture Kill"), PackSource.BUILT_IN, pack_format 34) added in AddPackFindersEvent via Pack.readMetaAndCreate (null result is handled: the pack is only added if non-null, TextureKillClientEvents.java:47-49). TransparentTexturePack.getResource() returns a generated 1x1 fully transparent ARGB PNG (generateTransparentPng, TransparentTexturePack.java:103-113) for every ResourceLocation in the list. The original file on disk is never touched.
  2. erase_regions → TextureRegionEraser, a PreparableReloadListener registered via RegisterClientReloadListenersEvent. On every resource reload prepare() reads the ORIGINAL PNG through ResourceManager, copies it into TYPE_INT_ARGB, sets the configured pixel rectangles to 0x00000000, re-encodes via ImageIO and hands the bytes to apply(), which puts them in the static CACHE.
- ONE pack serves BOTH mechanisms: TransparentTexturePack.getResource() checks config.getKilledTextures() first (line 60), then TextureRegionEraser.CACHE (lines 63-66); listResources() and getNamespaces() likewise iterate both (lines 75-86, 95-96). getResource/listResources/getNamespaces all bail out for PackType != CLIENT_RESOURCES; getRootResource() always returns null; getMetadataSection() only answers the "pack" section.
- Pack registration call is literally `new PackSelectionConfig(true, Pack.Position.TOP, false)` (TextureKillClientEvents.java:44) — the pack sorts to the top of the pack list. The exact meaning of the first/third boolean is a vanilla record detail, not provable from this repo (so "always enabled / not user-removable" is a reasonable but unproven reading).
- Reload ordering trick (documented in-code, TextureRegionEraser.java:28-31, 50-52): CACHE.clear() happens first in prepare() so the pack falls through to the lower-priority packs and the eraser reads UNMODIFIED originals; without that the erasures would compound on every F3+T.
- apply() additionally registers each erased texture as a DynamicTexture in Minecraft's TextureManager ("belt-and-suspenders", TextureRegionEraser.java:104-116) explicitly so mods like ETF (Entity Texture Features) that bypass ResourceManager still get the modified image.

GOTCHAS FOR A DOC WRITER
- Both handlers re-check module.isModuleEnabled() at event time (TextureKillClientEvents.java:31, 55). Both are MOD-bus lifecycle events that NeoForge fires during client startup (that firing schedule is NeoForge behaviour, not provable from this repo), so toggling `enabled` in the config at runtime does nothing until the game is restarted — a resource reload (F3+T) is NOT enough to arm a module that was disabled at boot.
- Conversely, once the module was enabled at boot, editing killed_textures takes effect on the next resource reload (the pack calls config.getKilledTextures() live on every lookup), and editing erase_regions also takes effect on the next reload (prepare() re-reads config.getErasedRegions()) — no restart needed in that direction. This asymmetry is not mentioned in docs/modules/texture_kill.md.
- Performance smell (not a bug report, just true): TransparentTexturePack.getResource() calls config.getKilledTextures(), which builds a fresh HashSet and re-parses every config string via ResourceLocation.tryParse on EVERY resource lookup that reaches this pack (TextureKillConfig.java:125-137, TransparentTexturePack.java:60). Same for getNamespaces()/listResources().
- Killed textures are replaced by a 1x1 PNG, not by a same-size transparent PNG. For atlas sprites or animated (.mcmeta) textures this changes the sprite dimensions; only whole-file entity/overlay textures are proven to work (the defaults are entity textures). Region erasing, by contrast, keeps the original dimensions.
- Silent-skip behaviour: config entries that fail validation are dropped without a log message — killed_textures accepts any String containing ":", erase_regions any String containing ":" and "@"; ResourceLocation.tryParse failures and unparsable @x1:y1-x2:y2 ranges are `continue`d silently (TextureKillConfig.java:131-134, 146-161). A typo therefore looks exactly like "the module doesn't work".
- Coordinate edge cases (traced through parseRegion + the erase loop): NEGATIVE START coordinates cannot be expressed at all — parseRegion splits on the FIRST '-', so a leading minus makes the start half unparsable and the entry is silently dropped (no out-of-bounds risk from setRGB). Negative or inverted END coordinates parse fine and simply erase nothing. The erase loop clamps only the upper edge (`y < y2 && y < img.getHeight()`, `x < x2 && x < img.getWidth()`, TextureRegionEraser.java:80-84), so oversized rectangles are harmless.
- Region erasing only works for textures that ResourceManager can resolve. resource.isEmpty() → silently skipped (lines 60-62); a decode failure (ImageIO.read returns null) logs a warn, an IOException logs a warn. Only IOException is caught inside the per-texture try — an unchecked exception would escape prepare() and fail the reload, but no config-reachable input produces one (see coordinate edge cases).
- Logging goes through the global Vpa.LOGGER (warn/debug), NOT through the module's debug-logging helper — so the module's own `debug_logging` config key does not gate these messages.
- The config spec itself is registered as ModConfig.Type.COMMON (VanillaPlusAdditions.java:131, StandaloneModuleBootstrap.java:45), so the `texture_kill` section also appears in a dedicated server's config file — but every line of behaviour sits behind @EventBusSubscriber(value = Dist.CLIENT) and client-only classes, so the module is purely client-side and inert on a server.
- TextureKillModule.onInitialize() is intentionally empty; everything is wired by the @EventBusSubscriber annotation. No shouldInitialize() override, no isEnabledByDefault() override (Module.java:73 default = true).
- No mixins, no items/blocks/entities, no commands, no keybinds, no lang keys and no resource files at all (grep over src/main/resources finds no "texture_kill"; the pack name "VPA Texture Kill" is a hardcoded Component.literal, so it is untranslated in all 6 language files: cs_cz, de_at, de_de, en_us, es_es, fr_fr).

MOD RELATIONSHIPS (why requiredMods AND optionalMods are empty)
- The module contains NO reference to any other mod: no ModList.isLoaded check, no compileOnly dependency, no shouldInitialize gate, no compat class. It compiles and runs with nothing but vanilla/NeoForge — which is why README's mod-dependency table correctly omits texture_kill.
- Create appears only as text inside the two shipped killed_textures defaults (create:textures/entity/train_hat.png, create:textures/entity/logistics_hat.png — TextureKillConfig.java:18-21). Without Create those two entries simply never match a lookup. That is a default-config choice, not a dependency.
- ETF (Entity Texture Features) appears only in a source comment (TextureRegionEraser.java:100-105): the DynamicTexture registration exists so that mods caching entity textures outside ResourceManager pick up the erased version too. The mod id is never named in code and is not verifiable from this repo. Without such a mod the extra registration is redundant but harmless.

CONTRADICTIONS WITH EXISTING DOCS
- docs/modules/texture_kill.md:40 says "The default list pre-configures ~30 regions". The actual default is 62 entries (across 38 distinct texture files). The "~30" may stem from the first default block alone (32 entries, lines 25-56).
- docs/modules/texture_kill.md:41 attributes the default regions to "Alex's Mobs Zombies Revamped"; the source comment (TextureKillConfig.java:24) says "AL's Zombies Revamped". All 62 default entries live in the `minecraft:` namespace, most of them under `minecraft:optifine/mob/zombie/…`, i.e. OptiFine-style CEM/random-entity resources that ship in a resource pack, not in a mod namespace. So these defaults target a resource pack's zombie/drowned/husk skins, not a mod id — consistent with the module needing no mod dependency at all.
- README.md:198-199 describes only the killed_textures half; region erasing is not mentioned in the README paragraph at all.
- README.md:308 links to `docs/texture_kill.md` while the file is staged as moved to `docs/modules/texture_kill.md`. Not texture_kill-specific: every link in that README list (lines ~300-309) still points at the old flat docs/ paths because the whole docs tree is being reorganised in the current working tree.
- texture_kill does not appear in the README mod-dependency table, consistent with having no required or optional mod gate.
